# Santhi School of Yoga & Vedanta Studies (Santhi Yoga India)

> A traditional Hatha Yoga school and yoga studio in Chirattapalam, Fort Kochi, Kerala, India, led by Master Aksharanand A S (known as Achu), who trained in the Sivananda tradition. Two-hour walk-in yoga classes run every day at 7:30 am and 3:30 pm, taught in English, for all levels.

## Key facts (updated 2026-09-23)

- Name: Santhi School of Yoga & Vedanta Studies. Also known as Santhi Yoga India.
- Address: Chirattapalam, Fort Kochi, Kerala 682001, India.
- Phone and WhatsApp: +91 7907714144. Email: santhiyogacochin@gmail.com. Website: https://santhiyogaindia.com/
- Daily classes: every day, no day off, 7:30–9:30 am and 3:30–5:30 pm. Some mornings the class is held at Secret Garden, an open garden nearby, from 8:00–9:30 am; message the evening before a morning class.
- Class order: opening savasana (relaxation), pranayama, Surya Namaskar, asanas for all levels, deep final savasana.
- Drop-in class: ₹500 at present — a limited-time offer on the usual ₹600. From November 2026 the class is ₹700. No booking needed. Mats provided. No packages or memberships; students who practise for more than a week get 30% off classes.
- Private session: ₹1,500 (₹2,000 from November 2026).
- Also offered: a separate meditation class (timing depends on availability), workshops in pranayama, mudras, alignment and Kundalini-focused practices, retreats in Kerala, online group and private classes, and a 28-day 200-hour yoga teacher training (€899 all-inclusive; 2027 batches in January, February, April and June).
- Seven-day residential retreats in Fort Kochi and Munnar run under the school’s retreat project, Samya Retreats (https://samyaretreats.com/). The 2027 dates are 13–19 March, 4–10 September, 10–16 October and 4–10 December, chosen so they do not overlap the teacher training months.
- Teacher: Master Aksharanand A S. Trained in the Sivananda tradition; holds an Advanced Teacher Training Certificate. Over fifteen years teaching in Fort Kochi, more than 5,000 group classes, more than 70 international teacher training batches.
- The school is not a Yoga Alliance Registered Yoga School; teacher training graduates receive the school's own certificate.
- The school is independent and is not an official Sivananda Yoga Vedanta centre.
- The school is not connected to Santhi Yoga International in Vagamon, a separate organisation.

## Philosophy

- [The eight limbs of yoga, explained simply](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/eight-limbs-of-yoga/): The eight limbs of yoga from Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras explained simply: the yamas and niyamas, asana, pranayama, the inner limbs, and each in daily life.
- [The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, explained simply](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/patanjali-yoga-sutras-explained/): What the Yoga Sutras are, what the famous opening lines mean, how the four chapters are arranged, and how to read the text without getting lost.
- [What is Vedanta? A plain-English introduction](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/what-is-vedanta/): What Vedanta is: the Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita and Brahma Sutras, its main schools, Adi Shankara’s roots in Kaladi near Kochi, and how Vedanta relates to yoga.
- [The seven chakras, explained simply](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/chakras-explained/): What the seven chakras are in the yoga tradition, where each sits and what it is associated with — without the mysticism or the sales pitch.
- [Om shanti shanti shanti: why three times](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/om-shanti-threefold-peace/): What shanti means, and why the Vedantic tradition repeats it three times: peace from within, peace from others, and peace from what we cannot control.
- [Vata, pitta and kapha: the three doshas](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/doshas-explained/): What the three doshas are in Ayurveda, the qualities of vata, pitta and kapha, how to recognise your own tendency, and how a yoga practice fits each one.
- [How to meditate every day: a beginner’s method](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/how-to-meditate-daily/): How to start a daily meditation practice that lasts: how long to sit, how to sit, what to do with a busy mind, and the traditional order that makes it easier.
- [What does Om mean? The sound behind the practice](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/meaning-of-om/): What Om means, where it comes from, why it is written AUM, what the Mandukya Upanishad says about it, and why yoga classes begin and end with the sound.
- [The four paths of yoga: karma, bhakti, jnana and raja](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/four-paths-of-yoga/): The four classical paths of yoga explained simply: karma, bhakti, jnana and raja yoga, how they differ, and why the Sivananda tradition practises all four.
- [What does namaste mean? And how to use it in India](https://santhiyogaindia.com/blog/namaste-meaning/): What namaste literally means, how people in India actually use it, the gesture that goes with it, namaskaram in Kerala, and a little yoga-class etiquette.
